title: Solo dev, Claude + Gemini: how I’m building a vampire/werewolf idle RPG that lives in phone widgets
author: sozkan41
selftext:
I’m a solo developer working on **Widget Fangs**, an idle RPG inspired by old browser games like BiteFight. You pick vampire or werewolf, your hero hunts while you’re away, and most of the game happens in iOS/Android home screen widgets, the lock screen and Dynamic Island. It follows your real night and the real lunar cycle (full moon = werewolves hit harder).

It’s Flutter + Firebase + Cloudflare, and honestly I couldn’t have built it alone without AI. Here’s what my workflow looks like:

**Code:** I use Claude as a coordinator plus several Claude Code sessions on Windows and Mac (app, server, site, iOS native). All work lives in markdown “package” docs with numbered items, and the agents pick items, run local CI and mark them done. The biggest lesson was to keep one source of truth. Early on, agents kept overwriting each other’s files until I made “commit immediately” a hard rule.

**Art:** Characters, enemies and UI icons come from Gemini. I batch prompts with a small userscript from a JSON job list, then a Python + rembg script removes backgrounds and exports webp straight into the app. The hard part is style consistency: the same character drifted from painterly to “toy/cartoon” between batches. What helped was a fixed style-lock paragraph in every prompt. Also, rembg erases dark details on dark backgrounds, so I generate on light grey instead.

**Sound:** Kenney CC0 packs plus ElevenLabs sound effects for anything custom. Short SFX are great. Long loopable ambience is still hit or miss for me.

It’s in early closed alpha, free, with no purchases turned on. If you want to try it: [https://widgetfangs.com](https://widgetfangs.com)

Curious how others handle art style drift across big AI batches, and whether anyone has found a reliable way to get loopable ambient audio.
